subject: Performance qualification + trial plan for AcmeRetail inference (latency, streaming, cost levers)
messages:
From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Moretti <alex.moretti@acmeretail.com>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-15T14:05:00-07:00
Subject: Post-call recap — performance targets & next steps

Hi Alex — thanks again for the call today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment before we spin up a trial cluster.

Recap of Acme targets (from our call):
- p95 generation latency: <= 120ms for short prompts (~32 tokens)
- concurrent sessions: 40 active concurrent users with occasional bursts to 80
- throughput target: sustained ~12 req/s, spike to 25 req/s for flash sales windows
- streaming: yes — need partial tokens within 30ms of begin-of-stream for UX
- quality: want parity with current hosted model (v1.3) for product descriptions

Key cost/perf levers we discussed to hit SLOs: continuous batching (lower per-token CPU), prefix/KV caching for repeated prompts, 4-bit quantization profile for the tail latency path, and a smaller low-latency model variant for low-cost fallbacks. We also mentioned routing by customer tier and region.

Proposed next steps (please confirm):
1) Redwood to provision a short-lived dedicated trial cluster (GPU-backed) with streaming enabled and a benchmark harness — target up within 48 hours.
2) Acme to provide 1) a 24-hour sample workload (anonymized), 2) a representative prompt set (15–30 prompts), and 3) a list of top 20 repeated prefixes for caching.
3) Redwood SE (Vanessa) will run two benchmark passes:
   a) latency-focused: p50/p95/p99 under target concurrency (40 -> 80 burst) with streaming enabled.
   b) cost-focused: measure per-token cost across continuous batching windows and with/without prefix caching and 4-bit quantization.
4) Deliverables: benchmark report (latency percentiles, CPU/GPU utilization, token cost estimates), recommended config (batching window, cache TTLs, quant profile, model variants), and a 2-week trial SOW.

Attachments: I attached acmeretail-slo-reqs.xlsx (your sheet), a short Redwood trial checklist (redwood-trial-instructions.pdf), and an example metadata payload format (acme-metadata-sample.json) — please confirm we can use those.

Would you be able to: 1) confirm the targets above, and 2) send the anonymized workload by end of day tomorrow? Once we have that, Vanessa will schedule the benchmark run and share results within 48 hours of data receipt.

Thanks,
Neha Kapoor
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
neha_kapoor@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0182

Date: 2026-10-15T16:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap — performance targets & next steps

Neha — thanks for the clear recap. Confirming the targets are correct. A couple of clarifications before you spin up the cluster: 

1) Streaming: we need to ensure that partial tokens are returned to the client within 25–30ms of the token starting to stream; our UI relies on early partials. If Redwood can meet p95 full-response latency of 120ms and streaming partials <=30ms we're good.

2) Cache concerns: some of our prompts include PII placeholders; we cannot cache sensitive prompts. We'll provide a list of which prompt templates are cachable. Default cache TTLs should be configurable per-prompt.

3) Fallback policy: in case of overloaded GPU pool, we prefer to fall back to a quantized variant with the same API contract and a user-experience toggle (reduced sampling temp). Please include a recommended degradation plan in the report.

We're shipping the anonymized workload to the SFTP listed in the trial instructions by EOD tomorrow. Procurement copied on this thread — they will need the SOW and trial duration to approve the test.

Thanks,
Alex Moretti
Head of ML Platforms | AcmeRetail Inc.
alex.moretti@acmeretail.com

Cc: Alex Moretti <alex.moretti@acmeretail.com>
Date: 2026-10-15T18:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap — performance targets & next steps (benchmark plan)

Neha/Karthik — putting together the benchmark plan and wanted to record specifics here so Alex has visibility into what we'll measure. I'll run two passes on the trial cluster:

Pass A — Latency & streaming validation (priority):
- Environment: 1x p4d-like GPU node (for parity), streaming enabled, network emulation to match Acme's region.
- Workload: 32-token prompts, 15 prompt templates, both cachable and non-cachable sets.
- Concurrency: baseline 40 concurrent sessions, ramp test to 80 for 5 minutes.
- Metrics: p50/p90/p95/p99 latency for first token, end-to-end generation; stream-first-token latency; GPU utilization and host CPU.

Pass B — Cost/perf exploration (controlled):
- Variables: continuous batching window (10ms/25ms/50ms), prefix/KV cache on/off, quantization profile (fp16, int8, 4-bit Qat-like), model variants (base v1.3, low-latency v1.3-small).
- Metrics: tokens/sec, tokens/second per GPU, per-token cost estimate, quality delta (BLEU/embedding-similarity on your eval set).

Deliverable: single PDF with plots and recommended config. My hypothesis: with continuous batching at 25ms + prefix caching for 35% of traffic + a 4-bit quantized tail-path, we should hit ~p95 110–125ms and cut per-token cost 30% vs baseline. If streaming first-token latency is tight, we can prefer smaller model variant for initial token then route remaining decoding to higher-quality model (hybrid routing).

Need from Acme: the cachable templates list and anonymized workload drop location. Also confirm whether downsampling of high-frequency users is acceptable during benchmarks (we typically simulate full concurrency but can shape load to match production characteristics).

I'll schedule the benchmark window for 10/16 09:00 PT (subject to your data arrival). Once complete I will post the report to the shared drive link and short summary in HubSpot.

Cheers,
Vanessa Ortiz
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
